w: Before his morning worship, Swamishri went for Thakorji’s darshan and the Smruti-Mandir of Shastriji Maharaj. While circumambulating the mandir, a group of 16 devotees and 5 sadhus from Surat were effervescently chanting the Swaminarayan dhun. They had accomplished on foot their pilgrimage of 375 kms from Surat. Swamishri welcomed them by showering rose petals and said, "Sahajanand Swami Maharaj ni jay. The group of devotees from Surat have accomplished their pilgrimage on foot. Maharaj, Swami, Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj are extremely pleased by your effort and devotion. For every step you have attained the fruit of countless Ashwamedh yagnas because you had remembered God and His holy sadhu. You have pilgrimaged by foot to Akshardham!..."
Using paper, styrofoam and cloth, a beautiful stage was created by the sadhus, parshads and sadhaks of Sarangpur.

The birthday celebration of Bhagatji Maharaj commenced in the morning with the singing of dhun and prayer. In his blessings Swamishri said, "Bhagatji Maharaj was born in Mahuva on this very day. Since his birth, he was born to continue the mission of Maharaj. He was wedded to service and attached to Satsang from the beginning... He had developed a strong bond with Gunatitanand Swami - believing him to be the form of Maharaj and that Shriji Maharaj was working through him. Bhagatji Maharaj talked openly about the glory of Shriji Maharaj and Gunatitanand Swami in Junagadh..."
After lunch, at 1.05 p.m., Swamishri blessed a group of 30 devotees who had walked their way from Radhu.

st.t: Birthday Celebrations of Bhagatji Maharaj - 1 March 1999
w: The birthday of Bhagatji Maharaj was celebrated from 9.00 am to 12.00 noon at the Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Mandir, Sarangpur. After several speeches by the senior sadhus, Swamishri blessed the assembly, saying, "... One should do what the Satpurush (Guru) says. He says believe that you are atma (soul) and offer devotion to God with the faith that He is the all-doer. If one resolves that one is the atma, will there be any arrogance or misery in life? Whenever someone insults you, you will not get disturbed. In fact, the words will rebound back... "Doing what God or the Satpurush tells you is the right direction (true north), otherwise doing things your way does not amount to having taken the correct decision. The easiest way is believing God as the all-doer and personally consolidating His preachings and instructions in life. Then one will not face any problems. So by accepting God’s absolute existence, total surrender to Him and obedience to what the Satpurush says - one will experience happiness, happiness, happiness!"
In the evening Swamishri attended a special dramatic performance of 'Karna's Enigma', performed by the children and youth members of the Sanstha.
In the evening assembly, Swamishri chanted the Swaminarayan dhun for peace to prevail in the spate of communal violence in Gujarat.
Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of murtis for a new Swaminarayan Sanskardham in the village of Ramangamadi district Vadodara.

From 6.10 p.m., Swamishri attended the 20th annual day celebration day of Shri Akshar Purushottam Chhatralay. After speeches and bhajans by the chhatralay students a youth performed a monoacting on 'Pibek's Defeat.' The hostel youths performed a drama called 'The Darbar of Dharmaraja' that conveyed the message that morality and spirituality are more important than money and power. After another drama 'A Summons for the Witness', which showed different elements responsible for the erosion of character in today's students, Swamishri blessed the assembly, " ... You must first be conscious that you are students. Your priority is to study and to develop character. You should overcome whatever faults you have. By looking at another's fault you can never improve yourself... The change should be inspired within yourself."

On the way from Junagadh to Gondal, Swamishri visited Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Jetpur for darshan. It was here that Ramanand Swami had appointed the 21-year-old Shriji Maharaj as his successor and head of the Sampraday. ( see photo story )
During Pramukh Swami Maharaj's stay in Mumbai, on various occasions children too kept offering devotion in different forms, from vows and austerities onwards, to please their beloved Swamishri.

Today Mayur Shashikant Patel (Chicago), Markand Soni, Jogi Dave, Ashish Mehta and other small children had on their own prepared a short skit. Mayur acted out Gunatitanand Swami's saying, "Laddus of poison taste good while eating, but after a while the throat chokes...", and the other three children, choking as if they had eaten poison and died, fell to the ground.
Laughing, Swamishri said, "What are laddus of poison?"
The children said nothing.
So Swamishri said, "What we eat from the market. So do not eat from the market, and keep your rules and dharma properly."

On the day of Mahashivratri, when Swamishri was having darshan of Thakorji, the boy Mumukshu Ajmera was singing the kirtan "Yogijine vandan varamvar...". In it he sang, "To give moksha to seekers you travel evening and morning..."
Hearing this, Swamishri said, "He travels day and night only to give moksha to seekers." Saying this, he then said, "To receive moksha, stop eating outside food and listening to outside songs."

On the day of Vasant Panchami, when Swamishri, after darshan of Thakorji in the mandir, came to the fifth floor for his morning puja, the kirtan "Ek ratre..." from the life story of Shastriji Maharaj began. Markand Soni, dressed as little Dungar Bhakta, was walking fearlessly with a stick, going round and round. The sounds of ghosts came from the background, and within a while these ghosts in masks crowded around together. The attempt to frighten Dungar Bhakta failed. This scene was briefly enacted and won Swamishri's pleasure. Swamishri blessed Markand and all the youths and teenagers who had become ghosts. Markand said, "Just like these ghosts, the ghosts of maya lie within us. Please remove them."
Swamishri said, "They will certainly go." Giving this promise, Swamishri went to his morning puja.
Swamishri naturally instilled in the hearts of small children the rules of pure food and living and high spiritual values.

Swamishri easily planted rules of pure food and conduct and high spiritual values in the hearts of the little children.
At 6.10 p.m. Swamishri left New Delhi and arrived in Bhavnagar at 7.20 p.m. Swamishri was welcomed with garlands.

The Pushpadolotsav (Fuldol festival) commenced at 5.00 p.m. After singing of dhun and prayer, senior sadhus discoursed to the mammoth assembly. In conclusion, Swamishri blessed the gathering and showered sanctified coloured water on everyone. (For details and photos see Swaminarayan Bliss, April 2010, p. 23 and back cover).

Today was the Pushpadolotsav. Pramukh Swami Maharaj had been busy since morning. Today Swamishri had given personal meetings to about 175 devotees, and more than 80,000 devotees had begun arriving from the morning to attend the festival. On such an occasion Swamishri too felt in his mind that the earlier he could reach the festival, the better.
And so, as Swamishri was going for his afternoon rest, Dr Kiranbhai Doshi asked him, "The time to reach the assembly is 6:00 in the evening, so do you want to take your walk in the evening?"
"We will see." Saying this, Swamishri cut the conversation short, but then he said, "It will be all right if we do not do it for one day, won't it!"
Dr Kiranbhai said, "If there is tension about going to the assembly even while walking, the blood pressure will rise needlessly, so what you say is better."

Swamishri said nothing more, but from 4:30 in the evening he sat insisting on going to the assembly. However, the weather had suddenly changed this time and it was intensely hot. So it was best that Swamishri did not set out now. Even so, Swamishri was firm. While reading letters, Swamishri kept talking about going to the assembly again and again. So, keeping Swamishri's health in mind, Dr Kiranbhai said to him, "The sun is very strong outside."
Looking towards the window, Swamishri said calmly, "I can see it too."
Dr Kiranbhai Doshi said, "It is just as hot outside too."
Swamishri said slowly, "What must be happening to the people sitting in the assembly?!"
Dr Kiranbhai said, "They all certainly feel the heat, but since you are there, you will protect them, won't you!"
Swamishri said, "If I protect those people, will I not protect myself?"

Hearing this, Dr Kiranbhai could not say anything and remained silent. So Swamishri said again, "The bodies of all the people sitting in the assembly are not made of iron or wood, are they! They must be feeling the heat too! They are all sitting there with faith, so what problem will there be for us?"
In the end, knowing Swamishri's wish, nobody said anything.

Seeing the car decorated outside to take him to the Pushpadolotsav (festival of flowers), Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "There is no need at all to decorate the car like this. Why do any decoration? It does not befit a sadhu, so do not do it. For us sadhus, the simpler the better. There is no need for any decoration."
This is Swamishri's constant preference.

After finishing his breakfast, at 8.44 Mahant Swami Maharaj set out for the murti installation ceremony. Munichintandas Swami said, "Dr Sanjaybhai Shah's father was diagnosed with cancer 6 years ago, but Pramukh Swami Maharaj gave his blessings, and for 6 years there was no problem at all. Now the trouble has started again, so he has prayed for your blessings."
Giving his blessings in special words, Swamishri said, "The blessings will continue..."
It was as if Swamishri had recharged the blessings.

ds.p: On the flight from Jalandhar to Delhi
w: Mahant Swami Maharaj was seated in a plane, coming from Jalandhar to Delhi. Viveksagardas Swami said, "In 1970, while going down at Piccadilly Square station, I said, 'The Air India clock is very nice.' Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, 'Is that so? Then let us go and see it.' Having already gone down, he went back up and saw that clock."
The attendant sadhu said, "Bapa had such interests!"
Giving a true understanding of his guru, Swamishri said, "No, he had no interest in it; he did such things to please us."
What a big difference there is between Swamishri's way of looking at the guru and ours!
